samples.summary: replaceAll stale-offset test only has a single match, so it duplicates the replaceActive test and never exercises replaceAll's multi-match reverse sweep against a changed document
samples.evidence: The new test at test/view/find-replace.test.ts:85-101 uses 'cat dog' with query 'dog' — exactly one match — so it passes through the same code path as the replaceActive test above it (a single replaceMatch). replaceAll's distinctive behavior (iterating matches last-to-first inside doc.batch to preserve offsets, src/view/find-replace.ts:89-93) is only covered by the pre-existing 'should replace all' test, which has no intervening document edit. A regression where the re-search fixed only the first match's offsets, or where the reverse iteration mis-ordered after a re-search, would not be caught. The multi-match case is the one the doc comment at src/view/find-replace.ts:72-84 calls out as data-loss-prone.

samples.summary: New tests assert only final document text; no assertion on matches/activeIndex after the forced re-search, so index drift from the added search() call is untested
samples.evidence: Both new tests (lines 67-101) assert only the joined inline text. The added this.search(this.query, this.options) at src/view/find-replace.ts:63 and :86 re-enters search(), whose prevIndex-preservation branch (src/view/find-replace.ts:29-31) can now point activeIndex at a different match when the document edit inserted or removed matches before the active one. Neither new test has more than one match, and neither asserts state.activeIndex or state.matches, so a wrong-match-selected regression (user replaces the wrong occurrence) would pass. Existing tests cover index behavior only without an intervening document edit.
searchedFor: read all of packages/docs/test/view/find-replace.test.ts for activeIndex assertions after document mutation

samples.summary: No test for the case where the intervening document edit deletes the only match, making the re-search return zero matches and the early-return fire
samples.evidence: With the added re-search, replaceActive/replaceAll can now legitimately find zero matches at call time (src/view/find-replace.ts:64 and :87 early-return). The existing 'should not crash on replaceActive with no matches' test (test line 133) never searched successfully first, so it does not cover the new transition from a valid activeIndex to no matches after an edit. No test in packages/docs/test/view/find-replace.test.ts edits the document to remove the searched text and then calls replace.
